Testing the Latest VLC Player on Ubuntu Is a Snap

I stopped using VLC on Manjaro when it became unable to correctly play HD .mkv files.

Now I use Baka Player, based on MPlayer and I could not be happier.

I had a bit of a problem with VLC, Nvidia and .mkv files picture breaking up but it was fixed by changing the output video module from automatic in advanced settings, I think. Either way if yours is working it doesn't matter.

I tried every setting I could think of to try and get it working at the time, but to no avail.

It must have been a bug in that current release of VLC, or a dependant package, as I just installed the nightly snapshot of VLC from the AUR, along with the latest versions of its dependencies that were available, and it all worked.

I probably could investigate further and find out exactly what combination of packages/versions was causing the issue, but it's not really worth my time, now that I have the lovely baka player for all my media needs.
